findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex for the same key can clobber file index / leak
findings.body: The whole-function lock was removed. Two concurrent builds for the same key (for example getOrCreateIndex racing with init) now both call bleve.New on the same directory. The second call fails with an 'already exists' error, or one index overwrites the other in the cache and the loser is never closed. Nothing deduplicates builds per key, so a concurrent build can fail or leak an index.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache without lock
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without taking cacheMu. The map is now written under a fine-grained lock from concurrent BuildIndex calls, and TotalDocs is also called from search.init's new log line. Reading the map without the lock is a data race and can cause a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write'.

findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in init workers
findings.body: Inside group.Go closures running concurrently, `totalBatchesIndexed++` is an unsynchronized increment and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigns to the outer shared `err` variable. Both are data races, and the recorded batch count may be wrong. Use a local err and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Eager Init uses the long-lived server context and blocks construction
findings.body: NewResourceServer now runs the full index build synchronously with s.ctx, which is cancelled on Stop. Constructor failure now aborts startup entirely when the index build or lifecycle init fails. Previously the error only surfaced per request. Startup time scales with the index size, and the backend/DB must be ready at construction. The PR also skips the postgres integration test rather than fixing it.
